components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--foreground); color: var(--background); padding: 0.75rem 0.95rem; font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 800; transition: transform 0.18s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background-color 0.18s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 0.18s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Evidence Chip
components.description: Source, review, category, and risk evidence marker.
components.css: .ds-chip-evidence { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; border: 1px solid var(--tag-border); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--tag-bg); color: var(--tag-text); padding: 0.25rem 0.5rem; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1; }

components.name: Marketplace Search Field
components.description: Search and filter input used in hero panels and listing filters.
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 0.375rem; font-family: var(--font-body); font-weight: 700; color: var(--foreground); } .ds-field span { font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-field input { min-width: 0; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); padding: 0.75rem 0.875rem; font: inherit; font-weight: 650; } .ds-field input::placeholder { color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--foreground) 58%, var(--background)); } .ds-field input:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.css: .ds-mobile-drawer { width: min(420px, calc(100vw - 2rem)); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius); background: var(--card); overflow: hidden; font-family: var(--font-body); } .ds-mobile-drawer a { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; padding: 1rem 1.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--foreground); text-decoration: none; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-mobile-drawer a:hover { background: var(--muted); }

narrative.overview: Killer-Skills should feel like a public review desk for AI agent capabilities: fast to scan, strict about what gets listed, and calm enough that users can decide whether to install. The surface is not a mascot-led community hub and not a raw GitHub directory. It is a classified marketplace where navigation, ranking, evidence chips, and install panels all point to the same decision: can I trust this skill for my workflow?
keyCharacteristics: Classification-first: every core route answers one browsing intent before exposing the full directory.
Evidence-forward: source, review status, risk flags, category, and install command are visible as product facts.
Compact but not crowded: cards are scannable, headings are decisive, explanatory copy is short.
Multilingual by default: labels cannot rely on narrow English-only spacing or hover-only disclosure.

rules.name: The Evidence Color Rule
rules.body: Teal means action, active state, or review evidence. Do not use it as generic decoration.

rules.name: The No Beige Rule
rules.body: Warm neutral backgrounds are prohibited. Warmth belongs only in the Review Gold accent.

rules.name: The No Tracking Rule
rules.body: Letter spacing is 0 across the public marketplace. Do not revive tracked uppercase section grammar.

rules.name: The Border-First Rule
rules.body: A 1px border is the default separator. Shadows are allowed only when a surface needs clear click or panel affordance.

dos: Do keep the primary IA to Home, Skills, Rankings, Occupations, and Categories.
Do treat official/community as source evidence, not as a top-level category.
Do show only marketplace-approved skills in public listings; D-level or ineligible skills stay out of Skills, Rankings, Occupations, and Categories.
Do use the detail page as the trustworthy installation decision point.
donts: Don't copy CocoLoop's mascot or personality system.
Don't ship a flat raw directory as the primary experience.

Don't use generic AI landing-page tropes: gradient text, decorative AI gradients, metric-heavy hero sections, fake trust badges, repeated tiny section eyebrows, decorative grid backgrounds, or nested card grids.
Don't hide critical installation or review evidence behind hover-only interactions.
